evidence.summary:
The example traces the final response cites, read back from Tempo: 4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b, 6661aabbc96f535480066bbe28c66e55, the cited IDs that match { name =~ "handle POST /api/(orders|payments)" && duration > 300ms }. A claim about an example trace is checked against the trace it names.
Trace 4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b:
- root span: webapp `POST /api/orders`, 17648ms
- services, outermost first: webapp, api-gateway, order-service
- spans with error status: none
- error origin (the deepest span with error status): none, no span has error status
- most own time (duration minus its child spans): order-service `handle POST /api/orders`, 12706 of 17648ms
trace 4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b: 3 spans, 17648ms
  webapp | POST /api/orders | server | 17648ms | starts +0ms | http 200
    api-gateway | route /api/orders | server | 15883ms | starts +2ms | http 200
      order-service | handle POST /api/orders | server | 12706ms | starts +3ms | http 200

- services, outermost first: webapp, api-gateway, payment-service

- error origin (the deepest span with error status): none, no span has error status
- most own time (duration minus its child spans): payment-service `handle POST /api/payments`, 2290 of 3181ms

  webapp | POST /api/payments | server | 3181ms | starts +0ms | http 200

explanations.The final response cites a slow checkout: Cited trace 4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b is in Tempo and matches { name =~ "handle POST /api/(orders|payments)" && duration > 300ms }.

engineeringReview: Supported: checkout trace 4715b7764646608b1a48f1b3a2cec04b is 17.648s, including 12.706s in order-service; payment trace 6661aabbc96f535480066bbe28c66e55 is 3.181s, including 2.290s in payment-service. The deterministic full-ID check passed.

Incorrect: the answer says user-service occurs in 10/20 checkout search results and payment-service in 6/20. Actual Tool Run 4 contains 12/20 and 5/20 respectively. The judge used a different nondeterministic search sample and did not catch this mismatch.
Unproven: all-route, job-level P99 and service presence do not establish user-service as responsible for checkout latency. No user-service checkout span was fetched to demonstrate that claim.

Scope: 20 checkout and 5 payment results are returned subsets, not exhaustive day-wide totals. Hitting the limit conservatively means possibly incomplete; it does not prove more results exist. Existing Agent feedback misleadingly states that the source held more.
Three empty reads remain: invented checkout/payment service identifiers and a guessed route label. TraceQL syntax was valid and there were no model-observation cuts.
